text:
Juraj Slafkovský has 12 points in 16 games and only two goals, and his stat line might be the easiest on the Canadiens to read. He's getting 5.7 expected goals' worth of chances and converting 5.1% of his shots. That isn't who he is; our range puts his true shooting rate closer to 13.7%. Goals tend to follow chances.

The assists, meanwhile, are piling up: eight in his last ten games, including the feed Nick Suzuki finished against Utah on Thursday. That fits Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, which had him in the 88th percentile among forwards in primary shot assists last season.

He's 22, wore an A this week according to The Hockey News's Karine Hains, and The Athletic's Arpon Basu wrote that the version of him from the Utah game "will need to be the version we see from now on." The worry is the other end: Montreal gets under 49% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating a lot against him last season. Our range: about 22 goals.
headline: Slafkovsky's shot is missing, the passing isn't
